nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.sniHint: Custom SNI for client connections (domain fronting). Only works with self-signed certificates (no domain). If domain is set, SNI must match it
nodes.commentHint: Free-form note shown in the node list and dashboard (up to 500 characters)
nodes.portRangeHint: Clients will connect to these ports
nodes.groupsHint: Users of these groups will have access to this node. If not selected — available to all.
nodes.sshPrivateKeyHint: Paste your private key (OpenSSH or PEM format). Leave empty to keep current.

nodes.rankingHint: Lower = higher in subscription. Drag-and-drop on nodes page will overwrite this value

nodes.customConfigHint: If enabled — this config will be used during sync instead of auto-generation

retireRelay.title: Delete relay
retireRelay.loading: Checking the relay and its dependencies…
retireRelay.onlineForce: {count} active clients are connected to the relay via L2TP. Delete the relay and disconnect these clients?
retireRelay.offlineSince: The relay has been unavailable since {time}. Delete it from the panel without cleaning up the server? The number of L2TP clients is unknown; MikroTik devices connected to it will lose connectivity.
retireRelay.offlineSinceUnknown: The relay is unavailable. Delete it from the panel without cleaning up the server? The number of L2TP clients is unknown; MikroTik devices connected to it will lose connectivity.
retireRelay.accountCountUnknown: The number of L2TP accounts is unknown.
retireRelay.changed: The preview changed. Review the new figures and confirm again.
retireRelay.neighborUnavailable: A neighboring node is unavailable. Deletion is blocked; the changes needed there cannot be verified.
retireRelay.neighborRefused: Node {name} did not pass the network safety check. Review it before requesting a new preview.
retireRelay.neighborRuntimeForeignChange: The node’s running network state differs from the state managed by the panel. Review the changes on that node before trying again.
retireRelay.neighborNetworkNotReady: The server is not ready: the panel could not verify the node’s network state.
retireRelay.protectedChange: Deletion is blocked: it would affect a protected configuration, or the panel could not rule out such a change.
retireRelay.previewUnavailable: Could not check deletion. Close this dialog and request a new preview.
retireRelay.outcomeUnconfirmed: Deletion was not confirmed. Reload the page and check the relay state before trying again.
retireRelay.newPreviewRequired: The confirmation is no longer valid. Close this dialog and request a new preview.
retireRelay.forceRequired: Active clients: {count}. Close this dialog, request a new preview and explicitly confirm forced deletion.

nodes.rebuildRemoveWarning: This removes L2TP and its local account copies from this relay only. Shared accounts are kept, even when removing the last relay. The preview is valid for up to two minutes.
nodes.rebuildRemoveBusy: Removal is blocked while sessions are active. No sessions are forcibly disconnected.
nodes.rebuildRemoveIpsecBusy: Removal is blocked by active IPsec connections, which can remain after PPP disconnects. Disconnect IPsec on the client or wait for the connection to expire, then review the counts again. There is no force option.
nodes.rebuildRemoveCountUnavailable: Removal is blocked because the counts could not be confirmed.
nodes.rebuildRemoveNotOwned: The panel could not verify ownership of the installation and account. Removal is blocked.
nodes.rebuildRemoveRefresh: The removal preview is no longer valid. Review the current counts before confirming again.
nodes.rebuildRemoveFailed: L2TP removal was not confirmed. Check the relay state before attempting it again.
nodes.rebuildRoleStateUnavailable: L2TP state could not be confirmed. Role change is blocked.
nodes.rebuildNodeHasLinks: This node still has cascade links. Use graph removal instead.
nodes.rebuildNodeRetireRequired: This relay has L2TP enrollment or account data. Use relay retirement instead.
nodes.rebuildNodeDeleteUnavailable: Node deletion is blocked because link or enrollment data could not be checked.
nodes.rebuildRoleChanged: The node role changed. Refresh the form and try again.
nodes.rebuildRoleBusy: The rebuild lock is busy or was lost. Try again after the current operation finishes.
nodes.rolePortal: Accepts clients and tunnels traffic through the cascade
nodes.roleBridge: Internet exit point, hidden from user subscriptions
nodes.roleRelay: Intermediate hop, forwards traffic further down the chain
nodes.countryHint: Country code for grouping on the network map
nodes.bridgeNodeHint: Bridge nodes are NOT visible in user subscriptions. Auto Setup will only install Xray (no Agent, no Reality). The actual bridge config is deployed when you create a cascade link.
nodes.portalNodeHint: Portal node — users connect here. Auto Setup works as usual (Xray + Agent + Reality). After setup, create a cascade link to connect to a Bridge node.

nodes.ipTypeConflict: A {protocol} node with this IP already exists
nodes.addPairedProtocol: Add second protocol on this server
nodes.siblingNodeDetected: SSH settings will sync automatically from the existing node.
nodes.siblingExistsHint: {protocol} node already exists at this IP — SSH credentials will be synced automatically.
nodes.nameAndIpRequired: Name and IP address are required
nodes.virtualSectionHint: A virtual node aggregates several real servers into one balanced subscription entry. The client's Xray core picks the best server based on the chosen strategy. No remote setup is needed.
nodes.virtualSelectModeGroupHint: All active nodes from the selected group are picked up automatically.
nodes.virtualSourcesHint: Only checked nodes will participate in this balancer. The client always sees one entry — Xray decides which source to route through.
nodes.virtualNoCandidates: No candidate nodes available. Create some hysteria/xray nodes first.
nodes.virtualSourceGroupHint: All active non-virtual nodes from this group will be balanced. Nodes added to the group later are picked up automatically.
nodes.virtualStrategyHint: How Xray on the client picks an outbound. leastLoad/leastPing require the observatory below.
nodes.virtualStrategyRandomDesc: Picks a random source on each connection. No probes. Good when servers are equivalent.
nodes.virtualStrategyRoundRobinDesc: Cycles through sources. Even distribution, no quality awareness.
nodes.virtualStrategyLeastPingDesc: Picks the source with the lowest probed latency. Requires the observatory below.
nodes.virtualStrategyLeastLoadDesc: Picks the most stable source (lowest jitter). Recommended for VPN. Requires burstObservatory.
nodes.virtualObservatoryHint: Xray pings each source periodically to evaluate its health. Defaults work well for most cases.
nodes.virtualObsDestinationHint: URL probed via each source. Should return HTTP 204 quickly. Default — Google.
nodes.virtualObsConnectivityHint: Optional. A probe is treated as failed only if this URL is also unreachable directly. Leave empty to disable.
nodes.virtualObsIntervalHint: How often to probe. Smaller = faster reaction, larger = lower battery cost.
nodes.virtualObsTimeoutHint: How long to wait for the probe before marking as slow.
nodes.virtualObsSamplingHint: How many recent probes to consider. More samples = more stable choice.
nodes.virtualFallbackToFirstHint: When all sources fail probing, route through the first source instead of dropping traffic.
nodes.virtualNoStatus: Virtual nodes don't connect to a server — they aggregate other nodes
nodes.sectionObfuscationHint: Salamander and Gecko hide QUIC traffic from DPI. Enable only if your ISP blocks Hysteria — may perform worse on mobile networks. Note: when enabled, the server is no longer compatible with standard QUIC and no longer a valid HTTP/3 server.
nodes.acmeDnsProviderHint: Available provider names are listed in ACME DNS config docs.
nodes.acmeDnsConfigHint: Raw JSON object for provider-specific credentials/options.
nodes.sectionMasqueradeHint: Masquerade modes from docs: `proxy` and `string` (`file` mode is intentionally not exposed in UI).
nodes.masqueradeProxyInsecure: Disable TLS verification for the proxied website
nodes.masqueradeStringHeadersHint: One header per line: key: value
nodes.sectionBandwidthHint: Server-side upload/download limits and client limit policy.
nodes.sectionSpeedTestHint: Enables built-in speed test responses for Hysteria clients.
nodes.sectionUdpHint: UDP forwarding behavior and idle timeout.
nodes.sectionSniffQuicHint: Advanced options from Full Server Config.
nodes.sniffRewriteDomain: Rewrite requests that are already domain-based
nodes.sniffPortsHint: Same format as Port Hopping: comma-separated ports/ranges, or `all`.
nodes.sectionResolverHint: DNS resolver settings used by the server.
nodes.sectionAclHint: Use either `inline` or `file` (not both). GeoIP/GeoSite options are optional.
nodes.aclInlineRulesHint: One rule per line. If empty, legacy default ACL rules are used.
nodes.aclRulesEditorHint: Inline ACL rules are edited on the
nodes.domainHintHysteria: If set — TLS certificate will be issued automatically (ACME). Also used in subscription URLs instead of IP.
nodes.sniHintHysteria: Custom SNI for clients. Works ONLY without domain (self-signed cert). If domain is set — this field is ignored.
nodes.outboundsAclLockedDisabled: Outbounds ACL editor is unavailable because ACL is disabled for this node.
nodes.hintDomain: Domain for SNI and ACME certificates
nodes.hintPortRange: UDP port range for port hopping (e.g., 20000-50000)
nodes.hintRanking: Lower value = higher priority in subscription
nodes.sshNotConfigured: SSH not configured. Auto-setup and terminal require SSH credentials.
nodes.xrayFingerprintPoolHint: The published fingerprint is chosen at random from the selected ones.
nodes.xrayFingerprintModePoolHint: Pick several; a random one is published and rotates when the subscription cache refreshes (per cache TTL).
nodes.xrayFlowHint: Only for TCP + Reality/TLS. Leave empty for WebSocket/gRPC/XHTTP.

realityGuardReason.tls: TLS handshake failed (TLS 1.3 and X25519 are required)

realityGuardReason.cert_name: the certificate is not issued for this SNI

nodes.realityGuardLocal: Decoy site is hosted on the node itself — no check needed
nodes.realityGuardUnknownDest: No eligible public REALITY target. Check the destination address.
nodes.realityGuardMixed: Only public destinations are protected; other destinations are skipped.
nodes.realityGuardModeNotifyHint: Report failures without changing the REALITY target.
nodes.realityGuardModeOffHint: Do not check this node’s REALITY targets.
nodes.realityGuardInvalidMode: Select a valid Reality Guard mode.
nodes.realityGuardInvalidTarget: Notify requires a public REALITY target on a managed Xray portal or standalone node.
nodes.realityGuardPaused: Reality Guard is disabled in Security settings.
nodes.sniScanHint: Scans the /24 subnet of the node IP for hosts that support TLS 1.3 + H2 — suitable as Reality destination & SNI.
nodes.sniScanNoResults: No suitable SNI hosts found in this subnet.
nodes.sniScanNeighborHint: Same /24 subnet as your node — ideal for Reality
nodes.sniScanOtherHint: Domain's real IP is outside the scanned subnet
nodes.xrayShortIdsHint: Comma-separated hex strings (0-16 chars). Empty string is valid.
nodes.xraySpiderXHint: Starting URL for the REALITY spider on active probe. Best left empty (REALITY uses a random path) or set to a realistic path matching your SNI (e.g. /r/programming/ for www.reddit.com, /search?q=cloud for www.bing.com). Avoid identical values across nodes — that creates a signature.
nodes.xrayWsHostHint: For CDN (Cloudflare). Leave empty if not using CDN.
nodes.xrayXhttpHostHint: For CDN. Leave empty if not using CDN.
nodes.xrayXhttpModeHint: auto (recommended), packet-up (strict CDN), stream-up (H2/H3), stream-one (single bidirectional stream)
nodes.xrayTlsSourceScopeHint: One certificate strategy per node — applies to every TLS inbound (main and extras).
nodes.xrayTlsSourcePanelHint: Masquerade under the panel domain — its Let's Encrypt certificate is inlined into the node config and rotated automatically.
nodes.xrayTlsSourceAcmeHint: Panel installs acme.sh on the node, issues a Let's Encrypt cert for the node's own domain via HTTP-01, and lets acme.sh's cron renew it. Xray hot-reloads the cert on rotation — no panel push needed.
nodes.xrayTlsAcmeInfoLine: Make sure the node's domain DNS A-record points to the node IP and port 80 is free. Auto Setup installs acme.sh, issues the cert and registers the renewal cron.
nodes.xrayTlsAcmeEmailHint: Used to register the ACME account. Leave empty to fall back to the panel-wide ACME_EMAIL env var.
nodes.xrayTlsSourceManualHint: Use a separate domain for the node and paste a full certificate chain and private key. The PEM is inlined into the node config.
nodes.xrayTlsSourceSelfSignedHint: A throwaway certificate is generated on the node. Clients must enable allowInsecure — testing only.
nodes.xrayTlsPanelDomainUnset: PANEL_DOMAIN is not set — clients will fall back to node domain or IP
nodes.xrayTlsPanelInfoLine: No certificate file is created on the node — the panel ships its current LE cert in config.json on every sync.
nodes.xrayTlsManualDomainHint: Set the node domain in the Network section above (it doubles as the TLS server name).
nodes.xrayTlsSelfSignedWarning: Self-signed certificates are easy to fingerprint and require allowInsecure on every client.
nodes.xrayTlsSelfSignedHint: Use a real certificate (panel or manual) for production deployments.
nodes.xrayManualCertHint: Paste the full chain: leaf certificate followed by intermediates, each in its own BEGIN/END block.
nodes.xrayManualKeyHint: Paste the PKCS8/EC/RSA private key. Stored encrypted-at-rest by Mongo and never returned via the API.
nodes.xrayManualKeyMaskedHint: An existing private key is stored. Replace it by pasting a new PEM block, or leave the *** placeholder to keep the current key.
nodes.xrayPemInvalid: Not a valid PEM block — check BEGIN/END markers
nodes.domainHintXrayManual: Domain used as the TLS server name and as the Host header for ws/xhttp transports.
nodes.xrayApiPortHint: Local port for management API (not public, default 61000)
nodes.xrayFallbackDestHint: Where to redirect non-VLESS traffic (active probes). Accepts port (8080), host:port (127.0.0.1:8080), [v6]:port or unix:/path. TCP+TLS only — Reality has its own dest masquerade.
nodes.xrayExtraInboundsHint: Run extra VLESS inbounds on different ports/transports — clients receive every entry in their subscription.
nodes.xrayRemoveInboundConfirm: Remove this inbound? Connected clients on this port will be disconnected on the next sync.
nodes.xrayVlessEncSub: Encrypt client traffic inside the VLESS protocol.
nodes.xrayVlessEncProtected: Rebuild protects this node’s client inbounds. Node Save and Link Apply cannot change their VLESS Encryption. Nothing was saved.
nodes.xrayVlessEncOwnershipUnavailable: Could not verify Rebuild ownership for this VLESS Encryption change. Nothing was saved; try again when topology state is available.
nodes.xrayVlessEncRebuildScope: In Rebuild, configure and sync client encryption on a standalone Xray node with no active links before making it a portal. Link Apply preserves existing client settings.
nodes.xrayVlessEncAuthHelp: Server authentication. X25519 gives a short key; ML-KEM-768 is quantum-resistant but its client key is about 1.6 KB. Changing the type generates a new key.
nodes.xrayVlessEncModeHelp: native — plain packets; xorpub — masks the public key part; random — the whole stream looks like random bytes. Usually native.
nodes.xrayVlessEncTicketHelp: How long a reconnect can skip the handshake: 600s by default, 300-600s for a random lifetime, 0s disables 0-RTT. Up to 86400s.
nodes.xrayVlessEncPublicKeyHelp: The panel generates the client key and publishes it in subscriptions. The private key is not displayed.
nodes.xrayVlessEncRegenerateConfirm: A new key will be generated on save. Clients will stop connecting to this inbound until they refresh the subscription. Continue?
nodes.xrayVlessEncRegeneratePending: A new key will be generated on save
nodes.xrayVlessEncNoteClients: Clients need Xray-core 25.9.5+ (v2rayN, Happ, v2rayNG) or Mihomo 1.19.13+. sing-box based apps do not support it: this inbound is left out of their subscriptions (unless enabled for forks that do, see Settings → Subscription → sing-box) and is not checked by probes.
nodes.xrayVlessEncNoteRefresh: After enabling, changing settings or regenerating the key, clients must refresh the subscription.
nodes.xrayVlessEncNoteFallback: Fallbacks cannot be used together with VLESS Encryption.
nodes.xrayVlessEncNoteMlkem: ML-KEM-768 adds about 1.6 KB per server to every subscription.
nodes.xrayVlessEncOldXray: Enabling requires a stored Xray health version of 25.9.5 or newer. Save the node first and wait for a health check, or update Xray if necessary.
nodes.xrayVlessEncFallbackConfirm: VLESS Encryption cannot be combined with fallbacks. Clear the fallback of this inbound?
nodes.xrayVlessEncHealthUnknown: VLESS Encryption requires Xray >= {minimum}; no valid version from node health.
nodes.xrayVlessEncHealthOld: VLESS Encryption requires Xray >= {minimum}; node health reports {observed}.
nodes.xrayVlessEncClientOnly: VLESS Encryption is available only on panel-managed Xray client inbounds.
nodes.xrayVlessEncEditConflict: Xray profile or stored health changed during this edit. Reload the node before saving.
nodes.xrayVlessEncDisableBeforeTypeChange: Disable VLESS Encryption before changing the node type.
nodes.xrayVlessEncExtraArrayInvalid: xray.extraInbounds must be an array of objects.
nodes.xrayVlessEncNestedFieldsRequired: Xray inbounds require nested fields, not paths.
nodes.xrayVlessEncExtraIdsInvalid: VLESS Encryption requires unique, valid extra inbound IDs.
nodes.xrayVlessEncFallbackConflict: VLESS Encryption cannot be combined with fallbackDest.
nodes.xrayVlessEncClearFallback: Xray does not allow fallbacks with VLESS Encryption; clear the fallback dest first.
nodes.xrayVlessEncEnabledInvalid: VLESS Encryption enabled must be a boolean.
nodes.xrayVlessEncAuthInvalid: VLESS Encryption auth must be x25519 or mlkem768.
nodes.xrayVlessEncModeInvalid: VLESS Encryption mode must be native, xorpub or random.
nodes.xrayVlessEncTicketFormatInvalid: VLESS Encryption ticket must be 0s, Ns or A-Bs (up to {max}s).
nodes.xrayVlessEncTicketInputInvalid: vlessEncryptionTicket must be a string of at most 32 characters.
nodes.xrayVlessEncKeyInvalid: VLESS Encryption key is invalid or unavailable — regenerate the key and save the node.
nodes.xrayVlessEncKeyStorageUnavailable: VLESS Encryption key storage is unavailable.
nodes.xrayVlessEncMlkemUnavailable: ML-KEM-768 is unavailable in this panel runtime.
nodes.xrayVlessEncInboundIdInvalid: VLESS Encryption requires a unique, non-reserved inbound ID.
nodes.xrayInboundUniqueNameHint: When enabled, the subscription uses just the label instead of "Node name (label)"
nodes.xrayInboundPortConflict: This port is already used by another inbound or the API
nodes.xrayInboundTagConflict: This tag is already used by another inbound

nodes.agentUpdateAvailableMessage: This node runs an agent older than 1.3.0. Older agents lose runtime users when Xray restarts. Update the agent on this node (e.g. via the broadcast terminal) to apply the durable-config fix.
nodes.portConflictDesc: Port 443/80 is used by the panel (Caddy). Xray on the same server must use a different port (e.g. 8443). Otherwise Xray will break the panel after a server reboot.
nodes.obfsPasswordHint: Same password must be set on both server and client.
nodes.statsSecretAutoHint: Leave empty — a secret will be generated automatically.
nodes.confirmDeleteCascade: Delete cascade link "{name}"? This will also undeploy it.
nodes.xrayGenerateKeysConfirm: Generate new x25519 Reality keys? This will overwrite existing keys.

settings.updateDesc: Update or roll back the panel to a selected version.
settings.updateUpToDate: You are on the latest version

settings.tabSystemDesc: Performance, caching, rate limits and SSH pool.
settings.tabSubscriptionDesc: Branding, buttons and client app behavior.
settings.tabSecurityDesc: Administrator, 2FA, API keys, MCP and webhooks.
settings.tabBackupDesc: Local and S3 backups, schedule, restore.
settings.tabAccessLogsDesc: Xray access-log collection and analytics. Disabled by default.
settings.tabMaintenanceDesc: Maintenance tasks, cache, counters and danger zone.
settings.tabMigrationDesc: Seamless import from a Marzban panel — old subscription links keep working.
settings.loadBalancingHint: Less loaded nodes will be first in subscription
settings.hideOverloadedHint: Nodes with online ≥ limit won't be included in subscription
settings.hideOfflineHint: Nodes marked offline/error by the health checker won't be served in subscriptions.
settings.gracePeriodHint: How long to remember a client IP after the last Hysteria connection. Larger values smooth WiFi↔LTE switches; smaller values catch sharing faster.
settings.hyLimitDesc: Realtime cap on the number of distinct client IPs that may hold a Hysteria session. Hysteria 2 only — does not apply to VLESS / Xray nodes.
settings.howItWorksDesc: Devices are counted by unique IP addresses. If user connects from new IP and old one was active less than {minutes} minutes ago — both IPs count toward the limit.
settings.subscriptionsTTLHint: Ready configs. Reset on node changes
settings.onlineSessionsTTLHint: For device limit. Less = more accurate
settings.subscriptionsPerMinuteHint: Protection from token brute force. Norm: 60-100
settings.sshPoolHint: Reuses SSH connections for faster operations. Saves ~200-500ms per operation.
settings.sshPoolKeepaliveHint: Send keepalive packets to prevent NAT timeout
settings.sshPoolDisableWarning: Disabling is not recommended. Without the pool, network instability can saturate CPU with direct SSH handshakes. Direct mode is now capped at 3 parallel connections, but the pool is more reliable.
settings.nodeAuthInsecureHint: Enable if panel uses HTTP or self-signed SSL. Nodes will accept any certificate when connecting to auth API. Disable for production with valid SSL.
settings.realityGuardHint: Off by default. Only eligible Xray nodes set to Notify only are checked. Turning this off preserves node policies.
settings.realityGuardSaveError: Could not save Reality Guard settings.
settings.homepageHint: What to serve at the domain root (https://domain/). Instead of a giveaway redirect to /panel, visitors see a regular page.
settings.homepageUploadHint: Max {kb} KB. After upload the mode is switched to Custom HTML automatically.
settings.homepageResetConfirm: Delete uploaded page and revert to default?
settings.totpEnableHint: Confirm your current password, then connect the new device with a QR code on the next screen.
settings.totpProtectedHint: Confirm your password here, then enter the current TOTP code on the next screen to disable or rotate.
settings.totpEnableVerifyDescription: Scan the QR code and enter the code from your authenticator app to finish enabling TOTP.
settings.totpRotateVerifyDescription: Scan the new QR code and enter the code from your new device to complete secret rotation.
settings.newPasswordTooShort: New password must be at least 6 characters
settings.passwordTotpNextStepHint: After password verification, you will be asked for the current TOTP code on a separate screen.

settings.happHwidExplainStrict: Same as Soft, but clients without the x-hwid header are soft-blocked at subscription fetch: they receive a structurally valid subscription containing fake servers whose names are the “No HWID support” text below.
settings.happHwidExplainSoftBlock: When a client that sends x-hwid exceeds the device limit, it receives the same soft-block: a subscription with fake servers named after the “Limit reached” text. HAPP additionally shows an in-app popup. No 4xx/5xx is returned, so clients do not break.

settings.routingDesc: Configure which websites and services your users access directly (bypassing VPN) and which go through the VPN tunnel.
settings.routingEnabledHint: When disabled, subscriptions are generated without routing rules — all traffic goes through VPN.
settings.routingHowItWorksDesc:
Routing rules are embedded into subscription configs delivered to VPN clients. When a user opens a website or app, the client checks the destination against these rules:
• direct — traffic goes directly, bypassing the VPN (e.g. local banking, government services).
• block — traffic is dropped (e.g. ads, trackers).
• Everything else goes through the VPN tunnel as usual.

Rules also configure Split DNS: domains matching direct rules are resolved via the domestic DNS server, while all other queries go through the encrypted remote DNS.
settings.routingPresetsHint: Presets are additive — click multiple presets to combine them. For example, "Bypass RU" + "Block Ads" will add both rule sets. Duplicate rules are skipped automatically.
settings.routingRulesHint: Rules are applied top to bottom. First match wins. Disabled rules are skipped.
settings.routingNoRules: No rules yet. Add manually or pick a preset above.
settings.routingDnsHint: Domains matching "direct" rules are resolved via the domestic DNS. Everything else is resolved through the remote (encrypted) DNS via proxy tunnel.
settings.routingDnsDomesticHint: Plain UDP DNS for direct domains. Empty value falls back to 9.9.9.9.
settings.routingDnsRemoteHint: Encrypted DNS for proxied traffic (e.g. Quad9 DoH: https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query)
settings.routingDnsRemoteDotHint: Optional DNS-over-TLS resolver. Used when DoH is empty. Example: tls://9.9.9.9
settings.routingDnsRemoteDohHint: Optional DNS-over-HTTPS endpoint. Takes priority over DoT. Empty DoT and DoH fall back to https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query.
settings.routingClientSupportDesc:
Full support: HAPP (native routing protocol), Clash Meta / Stash (YAML rules).
Partial support: Hiddify / SFA / NekoBox (sing-box JSON — some clients may override rules with their own templates).
No support: v2rayNG, Streisand, Shadowrocket — these clients use URI subscriptions which cannot carry routing rules. Users need to configure routing manually.
settings.routingIosDesc: Separate routing rules only for HAPP on iPhone/iPad. Android, Windows, and other clients keep receiving the default Split Tunneling profile.

admission.consoleLabel: Run in the provider console (not via panel SSH) and compare the line for the same key type
admission.verifyInstructions: Step 1 of 2: Compare this fingerprint using an independent trusted channel, such as the server provider’s console. Do not approve if it differs or you cannot verify it. The probe did not authenticate; approval allows SSH authentication only against this exact key.
admission.confirmInstructions: Step 2 of 2: Verify that the machine ID belongs to the intended relay, then confirm admission. This does not install L2TP or transfer ownership of an existing installation or accounts.
admission.revokeInstructions: Revoke the database grant for this relay? This does not uninstall L2TP. The panel will refuse if it cannot prove the installation is absent and no operation is pending.
admission.granted: L2TP admission confirmed. Installation is a separate action.
admission.checkUnavailable: Could not verify the relay identity. No approval was saved.
admission.challengeInvalid: This approval expired or was already used. Close this dialog and start a new verification.
admission.identityChanged: The server changed. Verify its identity again before continuing.
admission.grantConflict: Relay admission was refused because it conflicts with an existing grant or installation state. Check the relay and operator settings.
admission.legacySingletonInUse: The last database grant was kept so accounts and L2TP removal on the legacy environment-configured relay remain manageable. Remove L2TP from that relay or configure an explicit relay list before retrying. Do not delete the saved account directory.
admission.grantUnavailable: Could not verify the relay admission registry. Controls are locked until the registry is available.
admission.blocked: Relay admission is currently blocked. Check the relay status and wait for unfinished operations to settle.

messages.reconcileStillPending: The operation is still pending. No automatic retry will be made.
messages.reconcileManualBlock: Reconciliation cannot proceed with the current relay identity. The pending record is retained for manual investigation. Do not retry the change, reconfirm the grant, or edit the pending record.
messages.accountPreEffectBlocked: This request did not start any relay writes. An account intent was recorded; reload L2TP data to verify its status. Do not resubmit the change.
messages.accountReconcileRequired: A previous account change is pending. This request made no changes. Reload L2TP data and use the separate reconciliation action if available; do not resubmit this request.
messages.removeCleanupFailed: L2TP removal completed, but cleanup could not be confirmed. Do not repeat removal. Reload the data and verify the current state.
messages.reconcileInspectionUnproved: Inspection did not establish a safe outcome. The operation remains pending and controls stay locked. Do not retry blindly or edit the database.
messages.reconcileHostInspection: The relay could not complete the inspection.
messages.reconcileChapProjection: Could not verify the relay installation and managed CHAP state.
messages.reconcilePppInspection: Could not verify the PPP sessions.
messages.reconcilePidfdGetfdEperm: The kernel denied pidfd_getfd (EPERM) during PPP inspection. The reason for the denial was not determined.
messages.reconcileInspectReadback: Could not confirm that the inspected state stayed unchanged.
messages.reconcileUnconfirmed: The operation was pending, but the reconciliation result could not be confirmed. No automatic retry will be made.
messages.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard. Check your browser permissions.
messages.cryptoUnavailable: Secure password generation is unavailable in this browser. No account was created.
messages.runtimeForeignChange: The relay’s L2TP configuration was changed outside the panel
messages.runtimeNetworkNotReady: The relay server is not ready: the panel could not verify its network state.
messages.installRefused: L2TP installation was refused. Check the relay prerequisites and refresh its status.
messages.installBusy: Another relay or shared-account operation is in progress. Wait for it to finish, then refresh the page.
messages.installRolledBack: L2TP installation failed and was rolled back. Refresh the page before taking further action.
messages.installCleanupFailed: L2TP installation was recorded, but cleanup could not be confirmed. Do not retry; refresh and verify the state.
messages.canInstallAgain: You can install again if the updated relay row offers Install.
messages.installRecoveryUnconfirmed: Cleanup of the interrupted installation could not be confirmed. Do not start a new installation.
messages.installRecoveryNoState: No interrupted installation data was found for this relay. Refresh the page to see its current status.
messages.rateLimited: Too many requests. Wait before trying again.
messages.uncertain: The outcome is uncertain. Checking the current state; do not retry.
messages.canceled: The requested account change was canceled and not applied.
messages.requestClosures: Session closures confirmed by this request: {count}.
messages.created: The account was created. Use its reveal button to view the password.
messages.observationTimeout: The outcome could not be verified within five minutes. Controls remain locked; do not retry the operation.
messages.refreshFailed: The current view could not be loaded. Controls remain locked.

installChecks.KERNEL_MODULE_BLACKLISTED: A required kernel network module or one of its dependencies is blacklisted. Ask the relay administrator to review the policy; Install will not bypass it.
installChecks.REBUILD_LINKS_NOT_APPLIED: First create and apply a relay-to-bridge link
installChecks.KCP_LISTENER_UNSUPPORTED: L2TP cannot be installed while this relay has an mKCP listener. Apply a TCP-based transport for the link or remove the link before installing L2TP.
installChecks.XRAY_BASELINE_UNSUPPORTED: Install does not support the existing Xray profile format or routing layout. Reformatting the JSON will not make it a rebuild profile. Follow the instructions on this relay's card only for panel-managed profiles.
installChecks.XRAY_PROFILE_OWNER_UNSUPPORTED: An Xray profile has a file owner that Install does not support. Ask the relay administrator to verify who manages it. Do not change its ownership or overwrite it just to pass this check.
installChecks.XRAY_PROFILE_USERS_UNPROVED: Install could not verify the Xray user inventory or match the transit inbounds to applied links. Check the applied links and the running Xray user inventory with the relay owner before retrying.
installChecks.XRAY_RUNTIME_UNPROVED: Install could not verify the running Xray process or listener ownership. Check which service is using the profile and ports before retrying.
installChecks.XRAY_DROPIN_UNSUPPORTED: Review the Xray systemd drop-ins with the relay administrator and use a supported service configuration. Do not remove overrides blindly.
installChecks.PPP_MODULES_REQUIRED: Check that the relay kernel provides PPP and PPPoL2TP support and that the PPP device is registered.
installChecks.PPP_MODULES_PERSISTENCE_CONFLICT: Review conflicting PPP module startup settings with the relay administrator. Keep any settings used by other services.
installChecks.PPP_MODULES_LOAD_FAILED: Check the relay’s kernel module availability and module-loading policy for PPP and PPPoL2TP.
installChecks.NETWORK_OBSERVATION_REQUIRED: Ask the relay administrator to verify that kernel socket diagnostics, nf_tables, and XFRM are available.
installChecks.IKE_ACTIVE_RULE_220: Active strongSwan and policy routing rule 220 were detected. Identify which VPNs and routes depend on them and coordinate maintenance with their owners.
installChecks.RULE_220_CONFLICT: Policy routing rule or table 220 conflicts with this installation. Identify its owner before making any routing changes.
installChecks.IKE_ACTIVE_UNMANAGED: An active IKE service is outside panel management. Identify the VPNs it serves and coordinate maintenance before installing L2TP.
installChecks.XL2TPD_CONFIG_MISSING: The xl2tpd configuration is missing. Ask the relay administrator to restore the supported package configuration.
installChecks.XRAY_CONFIG_WRITABLE: Review Xray config ownership and permissions. The running service must be able to read the configuration without being able to modify it.
installChecks.XL2TPD_NATIVE_UNIT_REQUIRED: A supported native xl2tpd systemd unit is required. Check the installed xl2tpd package and service setup.
installChecks.PACKAGE_SOURCES_UNSUPPORTED: The configured APT sources are not supported. Check that they are supported Debian 13 (trixie) repositories, include the main component, and use the official Debian archive keyring.
installChecks.PACKAGE_INDEXES_UNVERIFIED: Install could not retrieve or verify the signed Debian package indexes. Check repository reachability, the relay’s system time, and the Debian archive keyring.
installChecks.PACKAGE_APT_PLAN: Install could not verify a safe APT installation plan. Ask the relay administrator to check the package candidates and confirm the plan does not upgrade or remove installed packages. Do not bypass the check or retry if the outcome is unknown.
installChecks.PACKAGE_SERVICES_UNSAFE: Package preparation found an unsafe service configuration. Check that IKE, xl2tpd and nftables are inactive, check who owns their units, and review their autostart settings. Consult the owner before changing an existing service.
installChecks.RUNTIME_PACKAGE_AUTOSTART_UNSAFE: Install could not verify the required Debian packages or confirm that package preparation was safe. Ask the relay administrator to check the packages and service autostart policy. Do not bypass the checks or repeat an unconfirmed installation.
installChecks.RUNTIME_NATIVE_UNIT_REQUIRED: Install could not verify that xl2tpd can be prepared safely. Check the Debian package, unit files and aliases, and whether either VPN service is active.
installChecks.XL2TPD_NATIVE_UNIT_CONFLICT: An existing xl2tpd unit conflicts with the supported native unit. Identify its owner before changing it.
installChecks.VPN_UNITS_MASKED: Check why the xl2tpd or strongSwan unit is masked. Confirm with the relay administrator before unmasking it.
installChecks.VPN_UNITS_NOT_LOADED: systemd did not report both xl2tpd and strongSwan units loaded. Check the installed packages and unit setup.
installChecks.HOST_PREFLIGHT: The initial host check failed. Verify the relay identity, PPP support, and installed VPN packages and units.
installChecks.HOST_BASELINE: The existing host setup did not pass validation. Review the VPN and Xray service and configuration baselines.
installChecks.HOST_CANDIDATE: The proposed configuration did not pass the host check. Review the current host baseline and the generated VPN and Xray configuration privately.
installChecks.HOST_INSTALL: A host check failed during installation. Verify the relay state and review the VPN and Xray service configuration before taking further action.
